messages.subject: plot results of fund() on mac
messages.subject_clean: plot results of fund() on mac
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am having a lot of troubles with the function fund(). Using the same .wav file sometimes it delivers an object sometimes it doesn't, it says NULL. I am using extracts that are at least 0.025 seconds long.

When I manage to get a result (table with x and y values) the plot is all white.

I am running a Mac with Mountain Lion and I have installed the extras needed to run seewave.

Any help would be very much appreciated.

Thank you very much.

Greta Carrete Vega

Université de Montpellier 2 (MsC)

messages.subject_clean: [seewave] plot results of fund() on mac
messages.body_plain:
Hi Greta,

what window length did you use to run fund()?
The default window length is 512 in fund(), so if your sampling frequency is 44.1kHz, it results in a window length of 11.6ms. As default overlap is set as 0 in fund(), there is only 2.16 windows for the analysis in a 0.025s object. If the fmax you chose for detection is not precise, fund() might be unstable on only 2 points?

Hope this helps.
I guess you might need to send you code and some .wav samples if you need more help.

Clementine

Hi Clementine,

Thanks for your answer.

Indeed, I use a window length of 512 and my sampling frequency is 44.1kHz, I have set the fundmax to 600.

fund(son,f=44100,threshold=15,fmax=600,ylim=c(120, 5000),plot=TRUE,from=0.6964357,to=0.7510581)

Should I change the overlap, maybe?

Cheers,

Greta

messages.subject: release of seewave 1.7.0
messages.body_plain:
Dear seewave users,

A new version of seewave (1.7.0) was deposited on CRAN some days ago.

This version includes, among others:

. ggspectro(): a new function to plot a spectrogram using ggplot2.
. synth2(): a new function to synthesize sound with envelope amplitude
and instantaneous frequency (tonal model). This function may be very
useful for those who need to modify an original sound or generate a
brand new one for playback experiments.
. ACI(): a new function to compute the Acoustic Complexity Index
following Pieretti et al. (2011).

Thanks very much to Laurent Lellouch for his contribution.

Some new examples are available on the webpage: http://rug.mnhn.fr/seewave.

Enjoy,

Jerome
